rowCoverage: The total includes pairs whose payee could not be classified as an organization. Only pairs with a classified organization appear in the public table.
title: Chains of dealings between one payee and one official
question: Where a City-paid organization and one official are linked by several kinds of dated record, in what order did they happen?
finding: 103 of 5,371 payee-and-official pairs show three or more different kinds of dated dealing inside two years; so do 19 payee-and-department pairs that include a gift, a lobbying contact or a hire. The commonest orders are: donation → approval → amendment (15); approval → amendment → donation (12); lobbying contact → approval → amendment (11); approval → donation → amendment (10). Where a chain holds both a gift, donation or requested payment and a decision, the money came first in 33 and the decision first in 42 (44% money first; screen 3 tests whether that is more than chance).
how: Every dated record from 2012 to November 2026 was laid on one line for each pair: donations to the official’s own campaign committee from the organization or from people who list it as employer; gifts and paid travel the official disclosed from it; lobbying contacts on its behalf; payments made, or received, at the official’s request; and contract approvals and amendments the official decided, sponsored or, as a sitting supervisor, voted on (Board files and the City’s contract-approval notices). A window of 730 days was slid along the line and the stretch with the most different kinds kept. Kinds that first appear on the same day are joined with a plus sign. Department pairs use contract start dates, Board files, gifts to the department or its staff, lobbying contacts and name-matched hires; chains made only of contract paperwork (19 department pairs and 0 official pairs) are left out.
limits: Each item in a chain is a public record on its own: a donation, a gift within the limits, a lobbying contact, a charitable payment at an official’s request, a contract. Large employers and frequent contractors produce chains by sheer volume: their staff give to many candidates and their contracts come up every year. A donor who lists an employer gives on their own account and may have nothing to do with its contracts. Organizations and officials are matched by name; a committee is tied to an official only when it is the candidate’s own committee, so ballot-measure committees an official controls are not counted. A sponsor is printed on 55% of the Board’s money files (regularly from 2014), and whether a supervisor sat on a given day is taken from the first and last day the records show them voting or sponsoring, not from a roll call of that vote. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
